findings.description: The security group allows SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance's administrative access to the entire internet, greatly increasing the risk of brute-force or credential-based attacks.

HTTP (port 80) is also open to 0.0.0.0/0. While this is often intended for a public web server, combined with the unrestricted SSH access it indicates an overly permissive security posture with no network-level restriction at all.

AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext inside the instance user_data script. This exposes long-lived credentials to anyone with access to the instance metadata, console, or Terraform state, allowing full compromise of the associated AWS account/permissions.

The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs does not configure server-side encryption (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving potentially sensitive network traffic metadata unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block / bucket policy
findings.description: No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy is defined for the netflow archive bucket, so it may be left with default or overly permissive access, risking exposure of sensitive flow log data. force_destroy=true also allows the bucket and its contents to be destroyed without protection.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, meaning data stored on this disk is unencrypted at rest, risking exposure if the underlying storage is compromised or improperly decommissioned.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of instances to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of instances to the internet.
